briefFidelity: FAILS THE GATE. The brief asks for two things at once: a transformation so large the work is 'almost unrecognisable between conditions' - 'two different weathers over the same terrain' - and a specific character to that transformation, 'sparse, broken and cold' under stress against 'dense, whole and warm' in recovery. Writing blind, before I saw the brief, I recorded what actually moves: 'Structure, symmetry order and primitive type are preserved across all three conditions - only size, alpha weight and warm/cool balance move.' Size and alpha are not sparsity and breakage. Nothing fragments, nothing drops out, no gaps open, the symmetry order never falters, and the element count looks constant across all three rows. 9190's stress state is the same snowflake with the same arm count, scaled down and dimmed; 9369's stress is the same disc-and-cog at half diameter. That is one weather at two exposure settings, not two weathers. The palette pole - slate and iron against ochre and copper - is the one part of the brief the work hits squarely, and I named both hues unprompted.
seedVariation: PASSES, but not comfortably. On the 120px sheet there are genuinely distinct families: three discs (9369, 9906, 10085), a snowflake burst (9190), a spiked star (9548), a chaotic pinwheel (9727), a diamond (10443), and scattered fragments (10980). Density spans two or three shapes up to twenty-plus. That is not one work twelve times. But four of the twelve - 9011, 10264, 10622, 10801 - collapse into a single read at browse size, 'grey triangle with small orange bits', and they are hard to tell apart from each other. A third of the collection sharing one silhouette is a soft spot, not a failure on its own.
thumbnailSurvival: Mostly yes. The two-hue scheme and the centered radial mass are legible at 120px, and the disc, burst, star and pinwheel families stay instantly separable. Two real defects: 10622 is low-contrast grey on near-black and very nearly disappears at browse size, which is a token that fails to exist in a feed; and all interior detail is lost - the small dark circles inside the discs, the copper squares on 9369's ring, the notches in 9727 - so only outer mass and hue split carry.
marketResponse: Visible, but it is not the claimed change, and it is inconsistent per token. The mechanism is scale plus saturation: stress contracts and drains toward grey, recovery expands and pushes copper forward. I saw that unprompted, so the axis is real. But the brief's axis is sparse/broken against dense/whole, and nothing in the sheet breaks. Worse, the magnitude does not hold across seeds. 9369 clears the bar - a bold frame-filling copper disc becomes a small muted token adrift in black. 9548 partly clears it, its spikes retracting into a rounder blob, the one place any structural articulation is actually lost. But 9011's neutral and stress states are near-identical: the same grey triangle, the same two orange satellites, roughly the same size. At 120px I could not reliably tell them apart. 'Unmistakable at 120 pixels' is a floor every token must clear, not an average, and the first token on the sheet does not clear it.
tokenIdentity: PASSES, and passes emphatically - which is precisely the problem. Every token is unmistakably the same object in all three rows. 9011 is the same triangle arrangement, 9190 the same snowflake, 9369 the same cog-in-disc, 9548 the same star. Nothing is replaced under drawdown. The work satisfies the identity constraint so completely that it leaves the transformation constraint unsatisfied; it has protected the terrain by never letting the weather change.
composition: Competent, with accumulating small faults. Focal hierarchy is generally clear - one dominant central primitive with satellites - and the alpha-overlap idiom is handled consistently. Against that: 9190 and 9548 clip the tile edge in neutral and recovery, and 10980's triangles are cut by the frame bounds, all ambiguous as to whether they are intentional bleed or accidental crop; 9727's center mushes into an undifferentiated dark pool where too many translucent layers stack; and margin discipline is erratic, with 9011 and 10622 sitting small and isolated in a lot of black while others overrun the edge.
reasoning: My blind description and the brief disagree on the one thing the brief says is the point. I wrote that only size, alpha weight and warm/cool balance move across conditions, and that structure, symmetry order and primitive type are preserved throughout - and I wrote it as a description, not a complaint, because the modulation is genuinely visible and I noticed it without being told to look. The brief then asked for the work to be almost unrecognisable between states, sparse and broken under stress against dense and whole in recovery. What ships is an intact object rescaled and recolored: the copper drains and the mass shrinks, but no element is ever lost, no gap opens, no symmetry fractures. Two of the four sampled tokens carry enough magnitude to read as a real state change at browse size; 9190 carries it only by scale, and 9011 barely carries it at all. The palette poles are exactly right and the identity constraint is met, but a transformation that is the point of the piece cannot be the part that is merely adequate on half the seeds. This is a permanent on-chain commitment, and the brief's own standard - unmistakable at 120 pixels - is one the collection does not meet token by token.
wouldChange: Make stress actually subtract rather than shrink: drop shapes out of the composition, open gaps, sever the satellites from the core and break the radial symmetry, so a stressed token is visibly fewer and fractured rather than the same object dimmed and scaled down. Then enforce it as a per-token floor - no seed ships if its neutral and stress frames read the same at 120px, which 9011 currently does.
